proof:
# Exact failures of capped positive merging

All coefficients below have absolute value at most one, include a fixed negative coefficient -1, and sum to zero. These examples refute particular positive-coefficient reduction rules, not any halfspace-depth conjecture.

## Exact probability evaluator

For positive coefficients p_1,...,p_k, let T be the k-by-k upper bidiagonal matrix with diagonal -1/p_i and superdiagonal 1/p_i. The sum X=sum_i p_i E_i is the absorption time of the successive independent exponential phases, hence

    Pr(X>=t)=e_1^T exp(tT) 1.

For independent Y=sum_j b_j E_j, averaging each matrix exponential gives

    Pr(X>=Y)=e_1^T product_j (I-b_j T)^(-1) 1.          (1)

All eigenvalues of T are negative, so the exponential integral is absolutely convergent. The factors commute since they are rational functions of T. Formula (1) also works with repeated positive coefficients.

For rational coefficients it is evaluated using only rational arithmetic. Start with v_i=1. For each negative coefficient b, in reverse order i=k,...,1 replace

    v_i <- [p_i v_i + b v_(i+1)]/(p_i+b),

taking v_(k+1)=0. The final v_1 is the probability. This is just backward substitution for (I-bT)v_new=v_old.

## Arbitrary small-pair merging fails

Take positive coefficients

    (9/10,1,1/40,1/2,1/20)

and negative magnitudes

    (1,31/40,9/20,7/40,3/40).

Both sums are 99/40. Merge the positive pair 1/40,1/20 into 3/40. The probability before merging is

    44654803616666020420209277/90424914060963166702617600,

and after merging is

    15380294780653175263/31144717777833976680.

The difference, after minus before, is

    45047868558815635573/219603362719481976277785600 > 0.

Thus an arbitrary merger does not necessarily lower the probability even under the capped constraints and with both a positive and a negative unit coefficient.

## Merging into the largest unsaturated positive also fails

Take positive coefficients

    (1,1,1,1/8,1/40)

and negative magnitudes

    (1,1/10,39/40,1/20,21/40,1/20,9/20).

Both sums are 63/20. Merge the largest unsaturated positive coefficient 1/8 with 1/40 to obtain 3/20. The probability before is

    2707328154118677286425321717654449/
    5529271691908209942614085489921600,

and after is

    1060866680607737867294402281/
    2166639116517141016477280400.

Their difference, after minus before, is

    314330359687274458483242667/
    221170867676328397704563419596864 > 0.

Every asserted rational identity is checked by `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_capped_positive_merging_counterexamples.py` using (1); no numerical integration is involved.
